newsitem.title: UK: Common Fund finances Cuban sugar, alcohol projects.
newsitem.headline: Common Fund finances Cuban sugar, alcohol projects.

text.p: Cuba is to participate in a project to promote alcohol fuel programmes financed by the Common Fund for Commodities (CFC), a U.N. affiliate, a CFC statement said on Monday.

The project, executed by the Group of Latin American and Caribbean Sugar Exporting Countries (GEPLACEA), aims at establishing the economic and environmental viability of sugarcane-based alcohol as a gasoline additive.
This would be in the context of reduced vehicle emissions and air pollution in urban areas, the CFC statement said. GEPLACEA is based in Mexico.
The CFC had also financed a pilot project in Cuba on waste treatment at factories producing alcohol from sugarcane molasses through recovery of saccharomyces yeast and biogas production, it added.
The pilot project concentrated on improving sugar waste treatment and using the waste for biogas, animal feed and fertilisers.
The CFC's Managing Director Rolf Boehnke recently held talks in Havana with Cuba's Foreign Trade Minister Ricardo Cabrisas and various high-ranking sugar officials, the statement said.
